items.summaryZh: 阿斯顿·马丁技术总监恩里科·卡迪莱在意大利大奖赛前透露，车队在匈牙利大奖赛推出的大型升级及荷兰大奖赛的后续优化，很可能将是2026赛季的最后一批研发，同时介绍了本赛季与2027赛季的发展规划。

items.originalTitle: 阿斯顿·马丁与本田公布2026-2027年F1研发计划
items.summaryEn: Aston Martin's chief technical officer Enrico Cardile has revealed that the team's major Hungarian Grand Prix upgrade package and subsequent refinements at the Dutch GP look set to be its final developments of the 2026 F1 season, outlining plans for this season and 2027.
detailZh: 阿斯顿·马丁在匈牙利大奖赛推出的重大升级包，以及随后在荷兰大奖赛引入的进一步改进，看起来将是其2026年一级方程式赛季的最后一批研发项目。
这是该车队首席技术官恩里科·卡迪莱的说法。在意大利大奖赛之前，他在车队《提前进站》访谈栏目的最新一期中，进一步介绍了阿斯顿·马丁本赛季以及2027赛季的研发计划。
以下是其中的主要要点，此外还有关于引擎合作伙伴本田在全年剩余时间里能做些什么的更多内容。
阿斯顿·马丁在夏休期前的亨格罗林赛道对赛车进行了大幅改造，引入了实质上相当于B规格赛车的升级。
这套包含16个部分的升级包包括一个全新的、更轻的车架和一套全新的前翼理念——在夏休期之后的赞德沃特站，车队又对前翼进行了调整，同时阿斯顿·马丁还引入了修改后的底板隔栅（floor fences）以及对扩散器小翼（diffuser winglet）的改动。
因此，车队在2026年以34项升级的总数并列排在升级榜第四位，但如果只计算性能升级，则跃升至第二位——仅次于法拉利。《The 比赛》估计，车队是今年到目前为止在升级方面投入最高的。
不过，卡迪莱表示，近期引入的这些部件将是2026年赛车“最后一项计划中的空气动力学研发”。
他说，唯一的例外是，如果阿斯顿·马丁在2027年赛车的研发中发现某些东西“值得今年在赛道上进行测试，以帮助我们的相关性验证（correlation）”。
“但就目前而言，没有安排更多项目了。”卡迪莱补充道。
接下来的一个月里仍会改变的是赛车的重量。
卡迪莱确认，阿斯顿·马丁仍然“需要完成我们的减重计划”，并预计这项工作将在阿塞拜疆大奖赛时完成，从那时起“我们将基本上在整个赛季余下的比赛中使用赛车的最终版本”。
虽然官方没有透露阿斯顿·马丁目前或之前超重了多少，但据推测，AMR26 的初始版本在最重时超重了 10 到 15 公斤。
卡迪莱表示，到9月24日至26日的巴库比赛周末时，阿斯顿·马丁将“非常、非常接近”重量限制。
当被问及减掉了多少重量时，他说：“这取决于你选择哪场比赛作为参考，但这是一个可观的数字——足以大幅提升圈速。”
“这是一项重大成就。有时候，它来自对个别部件的改动；另一些时候，则意味着重新思考最初的设计方式——甚至是底盘。这是小细节与大型结构构想相结合的成果。”
在谈到阿斯顿·马丁近期性能提升时，卡迪莱表示他理解车手费尔南多·阿隆索和兰斯·斯特罗尔所感受到的沮丧，并称“对我们来说，重要的是更接近于给他们一辆能让他们按照自己想要的方式驾驶的赛车”。
在实现这一目标之后——阿隆索在赞德沃特取得赛季最佳第九名，这是他2026年第二次获得积分——卡迪莱说：“不过现在，与他们之间的许多讨论都是关于展望未来。我们在问：2026年赛车的局限在哪里，我们如何确保在2027年再迈出一大步？”
但他表示，尽管赛季剩余阶段的重点将是利用一切可学到的经验来“指导2027年项目”，车队并不预期本赛季的部件会被用于明年。
“每一个部件都将是全新的，”他说，“所有东西都会经过改进。”
“但在概念上，它将是我们今年赛车所采用方向的延续演进。”
“我们现在走上了正确的道路，但我们并没有被它束缚。可以这样说：在着手2027年项目时，我们没有给自己设置任何限制，不会去考虑从前一款车上延续任何东西。
从这个意义上说，这将是一辆全新的赛车，这也给了我们实现目标的自由和心态。”
本田在荷兰大奖赛带来了规格2（规格 2）引擎升级——而且这是一次改进。卡迪莱说：“可以说我们实现了双步前进：原始性能大幅提升，可操控性也大幅改善。”
但本田的F1总工程师折原慎太郎也承认，可操控性仍然是他们最大的短板。
他在意大利大奖赛时表示，经过本田樱 设施（Sakura，位于枥木的研究基地）的工作之后，将引入另一项对策来改善这一问题。
但这类升级很可能就是本田在2026年剩余时间里所能带来的全部内容。
当在赞德福特被问及今年是否还会有进一步的硬件改进时，折原说：“这是今年唯一一次重大升级。”
“但如果我们找到了什么，比如通过小的改动就能提升性能的好方案，那可以摆上台面。但在2027年之前不会再有重大升级了。”
尽管如此，折原仍认为通过优化还能挖掘出更多动力——据估计，赞德沃特的升级带来了约10至30马力的提升。
折原在蒙扎接受The 比赛采访时被问及是否还有更多性能可挖时表示：“我们为这条赛道带来了一些标定方面的调整，以最大化我们的表现，但这不会是大的改动，只是优化而已。”
阿隆索表示，本田的升级“说实话并不是大的提升”——因为他和斯特罗尔在发挥这些额外动力时遇到了困难——但当The 比赛问他是否仍相信本田能重回与红牛合作时期夺冠的水平时，他说：“百分之百可以。百分之百。”
“本田投入了巨大的承诺。我们在日本的设施是最好的之一。我认为正如本田所说的，动力单元的人员和管理现在都得到了加强——而且之前参与过那个项目的所有人如今都再次加入了这个项目，所以我毫不怀疑，我百分之百信任本田。”
“我们只需要以某种方式缩短那个流程。”
detailEn: Aston Martin's major Hungarian Grand Prix upgrade package and subsequent refinements it introduced at the Dutch GP look set to be its final developments of the 2026 Formula 1 season.

That's according to its chief technical officer, Enrico Cardile, who has offered more about Aston Martin's development plan for this season and the 2027 campaign in the latest edition of the team's Undercut interview feature ahead of the Italian GP.
Here are the main takeaways from that - as well as more on what engine partner Honda can do over the remainder of the year.
Aston Martin overhauled its car significantly at the Hungaroring before the summer break with the introduction of what essentially amounted to a B-spec car.

That 16-part upgrade package included a new, lighter chassis and a new front wing concept - adjustments to which were made after the summer break at Zandvoort, where Aston Martin also introduced revised floor fences and a modification to its diffuser winglet.

As a result, the team has introduced the joint-fourth-highest total of updates in 2026, with 34, though it jumps to second on the list - behind only Ferrari - when only performance updates are taken into account. The Race estimates it as being the highest upgrade spender so far this year.
Cardile stated, though, that the parts introduced recently would be "the last planned aero developments" for its 2026 car.
He said the only exception would be as a result of Aston Martin discovering something in its 2027 car development that "makes sense to test on track this year to help our correlation".
"But as of now, nothing more is scheduled," Cardile added.
What will still change in the coming month is the weight of the car.

Cardile confirmed Aston Martin still had "our weight‑saving programme to complete" and that it expects this to be done at the Azerbaijan GP, from which point "we'll essentially be running the final version of the car for the rest of the season".
While there has been no official word on how much Aston Martin is, or was, over the limit, the suggestion is that at its peak the initial version of the AMR26 was 10-15kg too heavy.
Cardile said Aston Martin would be "very, very close" to the weight limit by the time of the Baku race weekend on September 24-26.
"It depends on what you choose as your reference race, but it’s a significant number - enough to dramatically improve laptime," he said, when asked how much weight had been saved.

"That's a major achievement. Sometimes it comes from changing individual parts. Other times, it means rethinking how something was engineered in the first place - even the chassis. It's a mix of small details and big structural ideas."

Cardile said in reference to Aston Martin's recent uptick in performance that he had recognised the frustration felt by drivers Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll and said it was "important for us to get closer to giving them a car they can drive the way they want".

Having accomplished that - with Alonso scoring points for only the second time in 2026 with a season's-best ninth at Zandvoort - Cardile said: "Now though, a lot of the conversation with them is about looking ahead. We're asking: what are the limitations of the 2026 car, and how do we make sure we take another big step for 2027?"

But while saying the focus for the remainder of the campaign will be to use everything it can learn to "guide the 2027 project", he said there was no expectation that parts from this season would be used next year.
"Every single part will be new," he said. "Everything will have been improved.
"But conceptually, it will be an evolution of the direction we took with this year's car.

"We're on the right path now, but we’re not tied to it. Let's put it this way: when it comes to tackling the '27 project, we haven't placed any constraints on ourselves in terms of trying to carry anything over from the previous car.
"In this sense, it will be a completely new car, and it gives us the freedom and mindset to achieve what we want."

Honda brought its spec 2 engine upgrade to the Dutch GP - and this was an improvement. "We've made a double step, if you like: a big increase in raw performance and a big improvement in driveability," Cardile said.
But Honda's F1 chief engineer Shintaro Orihara has accepted that driveability remains its biggest limitation.
He said at the Italian GP that another countermeasure to improve this would be introduced following work at Honda's Sakura facility.
But these kinds of updates are likely to be the extent of what Honda brings over the remainder of 2026.
Asked at Zandvoort whether any further hardware improvements were expected for this year, Orihara said: "This is the only major update for this year.
"But if we found something, a good solution to improve our performance by small modification, that can be on the table. But [there won't be] a major update before 2027."
Orihara nevertheless felt there was more power to be found - an estimate is that the Zandvoort upgrade provided a step in the 10-30bhp range - from optimisation.

"We have brought some calibration change for this track to maximise our performance, but it's going to be no big change, just optimisation," Orihara said at Monza, when asked by The Race whether more performance was available.

Alonso said the Honda upgrade was "not a big improvement, to be honest" - as he and Stroll were having difficulty exploiting the extra power - but asked by The Race if he still believed Honda could get back to the title-winning level it was at with Red Bull, he said: "100% yes. 100%.

"It's a huge commitment from Honda. The facilities we have in Japan are one of the best. I think the personnel and the management of the power unit now has been reinforced as Honda said - and all the people that were in the previous project, they are in again on this one, so I think I have no doubts and I trust 100% Honda.
"We just need to shortcut somehow that process."

detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿（汉密尔顿）在意大利大奖赛前分享了自己对成为首位在意大利夺冠的黑人法拉利车手的可能性的看法

刘易斯·汉密尔顿表示，在本周末的意大利大奖赛之前，他一直在考虑成为法拉利车队首位赢得主场赛事的黑人F1车手这一潜在成就的重大意义。
这位七届世界冠军在红色的第二个赛季中表现出明显进步，今年6月在巴塞罗那为车队赢得首场大奖赛胜利，帮助他保持争冠希望，目前他落后梅赛德斯的安东内利 59分，还剩11轮比赛。
汉密尔顿在蒙扎夺冠的希望得到了提振，因为Antonelli因超出引擎部件配额将受罚，从发车末位起步。

当被问及潜在的第107场职业大奖赛胜利对他意味着什么时，汉密尔顿说：“进入这个周末之前我真的思考过，我反复琢磨，只是想到我要来参加这场大奖赛这一概念的巨大意义，比如我甚至不知道我已经和迈克尔[舒马赫]在[蒙扎五胜]上持平了。”
法拉利车队的刘易斯·汉密尔顿在巴塞罗那-加泰罗尼亚大奖赛上取得了他身穿红色战袍的首场胜利。
“但我的前方还有第一次，意思是说，如果我有可能获胜，那将进入全新的领域。
“穿着法拉利的战袍首次在蒙扎获胜——我曾目睹夏尔（勒克莱尔）在2019年做到过，当时我和他一起登上了领奖台。但如果我能在这里亲自做到，那将是了不起的成就。”
"而一想到如果我真的做到了，我很可能是历史上唯一一位在意大利为法拉利做到这一点的黑人车手，也许吧，所以很多这样的想法都曾在我的脑海中闪过。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿和夏尔·勒克莱尔在米兰受到了热烈欢迎，法拉利车迷聚集在米兰，在House of Peroni Nastro Azzurro 0.0%活动上为这两位F1明星欢呼助威。
"压力很大。你也想为车队拿出好成绩。工厂里有那么多人，他们中的许多人将能来到这场比赛，还有大批涌来的车迷，那种热情是无与伦比的，你也想为他们拿出好的表现。
“我妈妈这周末会来这里，因为我想她还没去过蒙扎，而且还是在法拉利的比赛周末。我想让她体验一下，你也知道，让她把她能带来的所有好运都带来。”
引擎升级无法弥补‘全部差距’
法拉利本赛季第二次引擎升级的到来，应该会提升汉密尔顿争夺胜利的希望。
车队于周三确认，他们已经启用了2026赛季获准的两次引擎改进机会中的第二次。
也许法拉利本赛季最大的弱点就是他们的动力单元比梅赛德斯弱，而梅赛德斯同时也向迈凯伦供应引擎。
汉密尔顿说：“每一点帮助都很重要，我认为直到今年这个时候我们一直在损失，甚至在上站那条如此短的赛道上，整场比赛中我们每圈要损失0.4秒。这是一个巨大的差距，而且我们整个赛季到现在一直背负着这个劣势。
在F1 Show播客节目中，Harry Benjamin认为，尽管结果令人沮丧，汉密尔顿仍然可以从荷兰大奖赛中收获积极的东西。
“我能说的是，当我回到工厂看到每个人都在多么努力地工作时，我真的感到非常自豪。大家都在埋头苦干，每个人都充满热情。
“我看到今年的专注点和去年不一样了。去年，我感觉并没有一个真正的‘北极星’目标。我们尽了最大努力，但并不清楚我们究竟要朝什么方向努力。现在我们有了‘北极星’，我们知道自己需要朝哪个方向前进。
“我认为他们做得非常出色，真正地团结起来并交付了成果。这是向前迈出的一步，虽然还不是我们需要弥补的全部差距，但我们早就知道会是这样。
“但能看到每个周末都有新部件到来、不断改进赛车，看到我们在全力推进，这令人兴奋，我依然坚信我们具备夺冠的实力。”

detailEn: Lewis Hamilton shares thoughts about possibility of becoming first black Ferrari driver to win in Italy ahead of Italian GP

Lewis Hamilton is seeking his first Ferrari victory in Italy this weekend in Monza; Hamilton is hopeful a Ferrari engine upgrade will boost his chances; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Italian GP at 11.30am and 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1
Lewis Hamilton arrived at the Italian GP in a rare Ferrari F40 and revealed that the car's engine bore the same number as his racing number.
Lewis Hamilton says he has been considering the magnitude of potentially becoming the first black Ferrari Formula 1 driver to win a home race for the team, ahead of this weekend's Italian Grand Prix.

The seven-time world champion has enjoyed a much improved second campaign in red, with a maiden Grand Prix victory for the team in Barcelona in June helping to keep him in title contention, as he trails Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli by 59 points with 11 rounds remaining.
Hamilton's hopes of claiming victory in Monza have been boosted by the fact Antonelli will start from the back of the grid as he serves a penalty for exceeding his engine-part allowance.

Asked what a prospective 107th career Grand Prix win would mean to him, Hamilton said: "I've really thought coming into this weekend, as I pondered, just thinking of the sheer magnitude of the concept that I'm coming to this Grand Prix, I didn't even know that I had I was equal with Michael [Schumacher] on [five Monza] wins, for example.
Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton claimed his first win in red at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix.
"But the thought that there's a first ahead of me, in the sense that potentially, if I was to win, you go into new territory.
"Winning in Monza for the first time with Ferrari is something I've witnessed Charles [Leclerc] win in 2019, when I was on the podium with him. But to do it while I'm here would be phenomenal.

"And the thought of if I did do that, probably I would be the only black driver to ever do that for Ferrari in Italy probably in history, maybe, and so just like a lot of those thoughts have been through my mind.
Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were greeted with a big reception as Ferrari fans gathered in Milan to cheer on the F1 stars at a House of Peroni Nastro Azzurro 0.0% event.

"The pressure is high. You also want to deliver for the team. There's all those people at the factory, many of them will get to come to this race, the Tifosi, who come in huge numbers and the passion is unmatched, and you want to deliver for them as well.

"And my mum's here this weekend because I don't think she's been to Monza, but also particularly on a Ferrari weekend. I wanted her to experience that and you know bring any of the lucky dust she can bring."
Engine upgrade won't recover 'whole gap'
Hamilton's hopes of victory should be boosted by the arrival of Ferrari's second engine upgrade of the season.
The team confirmed on Wednesday that they have taken up the second of two opportunities they've been granted to improve their engine during their 2026 campaign.
Perhaps Ferrari's biggest weakness this season has been having a weaker power unit than Mercedes, who also supply McLaren with their engines.

Hamilton said: "Every little helps, and I think up until this point of the year we've been losing, even in the last race on such a short circuit we were losing four tenths a lap through the race. That's a huge deficit and we've carried that through the year to this point.
Speaking on the F1 Show podcast, Harry Benjamin believes Lewis Hamilton can take positives away from the Dutch Grand Prix, despite a frustrating result.
"What I can say is I'm really proud when I go back to the factory and see how hard everyone is working. They're really just heads down, and everyone's so enthusiastic.

"I see a different focus this year to last year. Last year, I felt like there wasn't really a north star. We were doing the best we could, but not really knowing exactly what we were trying to aim for. Now we have a north star, and we know where we need to work towards.
"I think they've done a tremendous job to really pull together and deliver. This is a step forward, it's not the whole gap that we need but we knew that would be the case.
"But to see bits coming each weekend, adding to the car, it's exciting to see that we are pushing and I strongly still believe that we've got what it takes to win."

意大利本土车手安东内利来到他的主场蒙扎，他清楚自己健康的积分优势在本周末几乎肯定会被蚕食，因为梅赛德斯为他触发了从队尾发车的处罚——他的赛车更换动力单元部件超出上限，这是本赛季早些时候可靠性问题留下的后果。

“这件事已经和车队讨论过了，”安东内利在周四的车手新闻发布会上被问及牵引气流（拖拽辅助）时说。
“而且，是的，我们已经在一些事情上达成了一致。”
"所以让我们拭目以待，看看这个阶段会如何发展。但如果车队要求我这么做，我会照做。因为，是的，显然，我不是在争夺……你知道的，当然，我仍然很乐意拿下杆位（通过做出Q3最快圈速），但，毕竟，我是从队尾发车的。
"所以，如果我能做任何事来帮助车队，我都会去做。"
安东内利表示，在意大利大奖赛从发车区末位起步意味着他可以更"享受"这场比赛。
拉塞尔表示，安东内利愿意帮助他，这很好地体现了梅赛德斯的车队文化。
这位英国车手预计将在之后的一场比赛中因过度使用引擎而接受自己的发车（发车区）处罚，有可能是在三周后同样适合超车的巴库城市赛道。
拉塞尔说：“我认为这恰恰展示了目前我们两个人之间的团队合作水平，以及托托（沃尔夫）希望如何运营这支车队。
我认为这对我们来说是一个非常难得且独特的机会，尤其是考虑到我们两人的经历——从一开始就都参与了这个（青训）项目。我认为这是我们至少应该做到的。
“上周（在赞德沃特）效果很好，如果角色互换，同样的事情也会发生。
“这周他愿意在排位赛中帮助我，这也很好。这就是我们作为一个车队的方式。
“我在未来的某个时候会接受一次处罚。什么时候、在哪里我还不知道。
回顾一下在意大利大奖赛上发生过的一些最具戏剧性的时刻。
不过，尽管安东内利的处罚让拉塞尔在本周末有机会大幅缩小与积分榜榜首的差距——他在荷兰大奖赛后已经落后59分——但拉塞尔强调：“对我来说，这不会改变任何事情，因为我一直想专注于自己。”
“专注于我的不足之处以及我想要提高的方面。”
“我一直说，无论我的队友是七届世界冠军、一名新秀车手，还是根本没有人，我的工作仍然是一样的。”
“所以，我这个周末的做法会和之前完全一样。”
拉塞尔在周五练习赛中做出了全场最快成绩，而主要专注于长距离正赛模拟的安东内利排在第三。
“他们现在是所有人都必须击败的车队”——拉塞尔盛赞迈凯伦，但仍对蒙扎抱有希望
尽管他们目前在车手和车队两个世界冠军争夺战中都处于领先地位，但梅赛德斯赛季初期的统治地位在最近几个月已被削弱，先是法拉利崛起，如今轮到迈凯伦走到了最前沿。
拉塞尔乐观地认为，蒙扎的高速赛道布局会比起过去两场比赛更有利于他们的W17赛车，那两场比赛都是迈凯伦赢下的，但他预计三支主要竞争对手仍将是巨大的威胁。
"作为一支车队，我们在最近六场比赛中赢下了两场，所以我们想说什么都行，但很快就会有答案了，"他说。
"我认为会有非常激烈的竞争。
基米·安东内利表示，他理解关于法拉利未来可能引进他的猜测会持续很长时间，但他坚称自己在梅赛德斯“仍有很多可以回馈的东西”。
“现在的势头在迈凯伦这边。法拉利本周末带来了升级。我们知道红牛拥有非常强劲的动力单元。说实话，我认为本周末的竞争可能发生在前四强车队中的任何一队之间——但我希望是我们。”
拉塞尔上一次大奖赛夺冠是六月底在奥地利，他补充道：“看看过去几场比赛以及兰多和迈凯伦的表现有多强的竞争力，可以非常公正地说，他们就是目前最需要击败的车队。
“我们知道我们的升级落后于大多数车队，我们希望过几场比赛后能重新成为最需要击败的那支车队。但目前，竞争是在迈凯伦和法拉利之间，他们本周末都带来了升级。”
detailEn: Italian GP: Kimi Antonelli to help Mercedes team-mate George Russell in Monza qualifying due to engine grid penalty
Back-of-the-grid start for Kimi Antonelli at Monza means title leader open to helping George Russell's bid for pole in Q3 on Saturday; watch Qualifying at 3pm on Saturday live on Sky Sports F1

Kimi Antonelli is ready to help Mercedes team-mate and title rival George Russell in qualifying at the Italian Grand Prix for a race the world championship leader will start at the back of the grid due to an engine penalty.

Italy's own Antonelli arrives at his home track of Monza knowing that his healthy points advantage is almost certain to be eaten into this weekend owing to the fact Mercedes are triggering a back-of-the-grid start for him by exceeding power-unit component limits on his car, a legacy of reliability issues from earlier in the season.
Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton both trail Antonelli by 59 points while McLaren's Lando Norris, the winner of the last two races, is 83 points behind.

Given he already knows he will start at the back of the grid whatever result he achieves on Saturday, Antonelli is open to aiding Russell's qualifying session and bid for pole position by providing slipstream assistance to the sister Mercedes around F1's fastest track to provide a straight-line speed and lap-time boost.
"It has been discussed with the team," said Antonelli when asked about the tow in Thursday's Drivers' Press Conference.
"And, yes, we have agreed on a few things.

"So let's see, you know, how the session develops. But if the team will ask me to do so, I will do it. Because, yeah, obviously, I'm not fighting for... You know, of course, I will still be happy to do pole [by setting the fastest Q3 time], but, of course, I'm starting at the back.
"So, if I could do anything to help the team, I will do it."
Kimi Antonelli says starting at the back of the grid in the Italian GP means he can 'enjoy' the race more.
Russell said the fact Antonelli was willing to help him out reflected well on Mercedes' culture.
The Briton is expected to take his own grid penalty for excessive engine usage at a later race, potentially at a similarly-overtaking-friendly Baku City Circuit in three weeks' time.
Russell said: "I think it just goes to show the level of teamwork we have at the moment between the two of us and how Toto [Wolff] wants to operate this team.

"I think that is a very good and unique opportunity for us, especially considering where we've both come from, being part of the [junior] programme from the very beginning. I think it's the least we should be doing.
"Last week [at Zandvoort] it worked well and if the roles were reversed, the same would have happened.
"This week he's willing to help me out in qualifying, which is great as well. That's just the way we are as a team.
"I will be taking a penalty at some point in the future. When and where I don't know."
Look back at some of the most dramatic moments to have taken place at the Italian Grand Prix.

But while Antonelli's penalty offers him a big chance to make up potentially significant title ground this weekend after falling 59 points behind at the Dutch Grand Prix, Russell stressed: "For me it doesn't change anything because I always want to focus on myself.
"Focus on my limitations and the areas I want to improve.
"I always said, it doesn't matter if I have a seven-time world champion as my team-mate, a rookie, or nobody, the job is still the same.
"So my approach will be exactly the same here this weekend."
Russell set the Friday practice pace with Antonelli, who mostly focused on long race runs, third.
'They are the team to beat right now' - Russell talks up McLaren but hopeful for Monza
While they continue to lead both world championship races, Mercedes' early-season dominance has been eroded in recent months with first Ferrari and now McLaren coming to the fore.

Russell is optimistic the high-speed Monza layout will be more favourable to their W17 than either of the last two races, which were won by McLaren, but expects all three of their chief rivals to remain big threats.
"As a team, we've won two races in the last six so we can say all we want but we'll soon find out," he said.
"I think there will be a lot of tough competition.
Kimi Antonelli says he understands the likely long-running speculation that Ferrari will make a move for him in the future, but insists he 'still has a lot to give back' at Mercedes.

"The momentum is with McLaren right now. Ferrari have upgrades this weekend. We know Red Bull have a very strong power unit. I honestly think this weekend it can be between any of the top four teams - but I hope it's us."

Russell, whose last Grand Prix win came in Austria at the end of June, added: "When you look at the past couple of races and how competitive Lando and McLaren have been, it's definitely very fair to say that they are the team to beat right now.

"We know we're an upgrade behind most and we hope we can go back to being the team to beat in a couple of races' time. But, for now, the fight [is] between McLaren and Ferrari, who have got the upgrades this weekend.

detailZh: 兰多·诺里斯透露，在意大利大奖赛前与迈凯伦签署新合同之前，曾有过其他'机会'。
天空体育F1的马丁·布伦德尔采访了兰多·诺里斯，谈论他的新迈凯伦合同以及总冠军争夺战，这次采访将在本周末播出；请在天空体育F1观看意大利大奖赛周五练习赛，直播时间为上午11点30分和下午3点。
观看兰多·诺里斯迄今为止跌宕起伏的赛季，其中出现了多次退赛和多场分站冠军，使他处于争夺总冠军的行列之中。
兰多·诺里斯透露，在签署新合同留在迈凯伦至少到2030年底之前，他还有其他的机会。
诺里斯已经赢下了最近两场一级方程式比赛，自2019年首次亮相F1以来一直效力迈凯伦。他表示这份合同“可能是我签过的最容易下的决定”。
不过，这位26岁的车手在接受天空体育F1主持人马丁·布伦德尔将于本周末意大利大奖赛期间播出的广泛访谈中承认，确实还有其他选择。

“当然有机会。但那是一种积极的机会。有时候，机会是需要去赌一把的，”他说。
“就我个人而言，我是一个宁愿经历一两年艰难岁月，也不要立即取得成功的车手——就像几年前我在迈凯伦所做的那样。
“尽管我渴望每一年都能夺冠，但并不是所有事情都在于我明天就必须加入一支能在下一场比赛就获胜的车队，去做这个、做那个。”
伯尼·柯林斯在《The F1 Show》播客节目中表示，她认为兰多·诺里斯在最近连续两站获胜、状态提升之后，仍然处于总冠军争夺战之中。
诺里斯指出，迈凯伦拥有一支由车队领队扎克·布朗和安德烈亚·斯特拉率领的“强大”团队，这是他留在这支位于沃金的车队的一个关键原因。
他补充道：“其中很重要的一部分也是我开不开心？即使在我们没有赢的时候，我也很乐意留在迈凯伦，因为我依然拥有一个绝佳的机会，依然能做我热爱的工作，四处旅行并做所有这些事情。所以对我来说，并非一切都关乎极致的表现。很重要而且很大的一部分是我身边的人。
“仅仅是因为我感觉自己像在家里一样，而且我很享受这一切。这几乎和说‘我必须留在一支能够保持竞争力并赢得总冠军的车队’具有同样的分量。”
克雷格·斯莱特讨论荷兰大奖赛之后最热门的话题，包括兰多·诺里斯是否仍有争夺总冠军的机会
诺里斯目前状态正佳，他在匈牙利和荷兰最近两场大奖赛中都拿下杆位并夺冠，将他与总冠军领跑者安东内利的积分差距缩小到83分。
本周日他还有一次好机会，因为安东内利由于超出引擎使用配额而受到发车处罚，将从队尾发车。
不过，迈凯伦仍将面临挑战，需要击败拉塞尔，以及法拉利的汉密尔顿和勒克莱尔，他们两人都换上了升级版发动机。
汉密尔顿和勒克莱尔在蒙扎将获得车迷（意大利铁杆车迷，即tifosi）的巨大支持，那里拥有最具标志性的颁奖台，俯瞰着主直道，赛后还会有数千名车迷聚集。
法拉利为在蒙扎举行的F1意大利大奖赛发布了特别版涂装，向迈克尔·舒马赫致敬。
布伦德尔指出，汉密尔顿此前曾表示，在实现加入法拉利的“梦想”之前，他会留在梅赛德斯，并询问诺里斯将来是否会考虑加入这支车队。
这位迈凯伦车手说：“这不是我现在想考虑的事情。从小时候起，你总会想象自己处在不同的位置。”
“我的梦想一直是留在迈凯伦。这就是为什么我觉得自己现在处在一个非常幸运的位置。但你总想体验另一边的情况，无论是法拉利、其他车队，还是梅赛德斯。”
“这就是人性。我认为你会想去体验处于这个位置和那个位置是什么感觉。”
兰多·诺里斯与天空体育的罗布·琼斯坐下来，畅谈他与迈凯伦签下多年续约合同、延长留队时间的事宜
"另外，还有其他车队的历史。刘易斯当年也是从迈凯伦去了梅赛德斯，然后又去了法拉利，我觉得尝试不同的东西、体验不同的经历其实也挺酷的。"
“目前，我会说我没有去想这件事。但请在2030年底再问我一次。”

Lando Norris has revealed he had other opportunities before signing a new contract to stay at McLaren until at least the end of 2030.
Norris, who has won the last two Formula 1 races, has been with McLaren since making his F1 debut in 2019 and says the contract was "probably the easiest contract I've had to sign".
The 26-year-old admitted though, in a wide-ranging interview with Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle which will air at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix, that there were other options.

"There was opportunity of course. But opportunity that is positive. There's opportunities to gamble at times," he said.
"I'm a driver that personally I would take one or two tougher years over instant success - as I did a few years ago with McLaren.
"As much as I want to win every single year, not everything is about I need to be with a team tomorrow that's going to win the next race and do this and do that."
Speaking on The F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins believes Lando Norris is still in the title fight after his recent improvement with two back-to-back wins
Norris pointed to the "strong" group of people at McLaren, led by team bosses Zak Brown and Andrea Stella, as a key reason to stay at the Woking-based outfit.

He added: "A good amount of it is also am I just happy? I was happy to be with McLaren even when we weren't winning because I'm still in an amazing opportunity and I still get to do the job I love and travel and do all these things. So not everything to me is about ultimate performance. A lot of it and a big part of it is the people that I'm with.
"Just the fact I feel I'm at home and I'm enjoying it. And that almost has enough control as saying 'I need to be with a team that is going to be performing and winning championships'."
Craig Slater discusses the biggest talking points off the back of the Dutch Grand Prix, including if the championship chase is still on for Lando Norris

Norris is currently in great form after claiming pole position and the win at the last two Grands Prix in Hungary and the Netherlands to cut his deficit to championship leader Kimi Antonelli to 83 points.
He has another good opportunity this Sunday as Antonelli will start at the back of the field due to grid penalties for exceeding his engine allocation.
But, McLaren will still have the challenge of beating George Russell plus Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, who both have upgraded engines.
Hamilton and Leclerc will have huge support from the Tifosi at Monza, which features the most iconic podium as it overlooks the main straight and thousands of fans post-race.
Ferrari has unveiled its one-off livery, paying tribute to Michael Schumacher, for the Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix at Monza.

Brundle pointed out Hamilton had previously stated he would stay at Mercedes before achieving his "dream" of joining Ferrari and asked if Norris would ever consider joining the Scuderia in the future.
The McLaren driver said: "That's not something I want to think about for now. Since I was a kid, you always think of yourself in different positions.

"My dream was always to be with McLaren. That's why I feel like I'm in a very fortunate position as I am. But you always want to experience the other side of things, whether that is Ferrari or other teams and Mercedes.
"It's just human. I think that you want to experience what it's like to be in this position and that position.
Lando Norris sits down with Sky Sports' Rob Jones to discuss extending his stay with McLaren in a multi-year contract extension

"Also, the history of other teams. The fact Lewis also went to Mercedes from McLaren and then to Ferrari, I think it's also pretty cool that you try different things and you experience different stuff.
"For now, I'll say I'm not thinking of it. But ask me again at the end of 2030."

“这就是我的方式——我们要说的是数十万，实际上说的是数百万——我要把我的整个体系、我的支持、我的知识整合起来，努力让尽可能多的其他人，尤其是某些车手，也有机会实现他们的目标。”

Lando Norris has launched a new junior single-seater team, LN4 Fusion, which will race in multiple championships in 2027.
LN4 Fusion has acquired selected assets of Formula 3 team AIX Racing to race in the championship next year and is undertaking the relevant application procedure to compete in Formula 2 in the future.

"I'm very excited. This is one of my biggest things I've ever been part of that's not just within my own stuff of Formula 1. Norris told Sky Sports F1 ahead of this weekend's Italian Grand Prix.
"[It's] my very own race team that I co-founded. So I'll be having my own race team in all the junior series.

"Obviously, we want it to be the best. We want it to be the leading single-seater race team. But it's just very cool to be part of something new, create something, and for me to be part of something for such a long period of time as well."

Alongside LN4 Fusion, Norris is also launching the LN4 Legacy Programme - an independent, fully funded driver development programme, operated by ADD Management and led by experienced programme director Julian Rouse.
The programme aims to identify and support future talent for those who do not have the finances to move up the motorsport ladder.

"The main objective of this is simply to help younger drivers who have talent and have the ability to get to Formula 1, but probably not financially [the ability], and help them in all those other areas reach their end goal," said Norris.

"Basically my little way of trying to give back, again, using my team, using the people that I'm with, my partners, and give other people, give young drivers a chance. So that's my more personal side of things, which is pretty cool too."

LN4 Fusion's principal European headquarters will be based in Veneto in Italy where a new facility is being built with a British operation in Cambridgeshire.
Norris added: "I was very lucky growing up that my dad could support me all the way through to Formula 2.

"But I know that there are a lot of other drivers out there who probably can get to Formula 1, but don't have the financial backing or the ability to know how to go through the whole programme, which is where the team comes into place too.

"This is my way, and we're talking hundreds of thousands, we're talking millions, in fact, of how I can bring my whole infrastructure together, my support, my knowledge, and try to give as many other people and certain other drivers opportunities to reach their goal too."

鉴于这两位英国车手落后 Antonelli 的差距相当显著，法拉利或迈凯伦是否会考虑尽早实施车队指令，以帮助他们在总冠军争夺中位置更有利的那位车手，这已成为人们猜测的话题。

作为劳伦斯学院成员接受 天空体育 News 采访的 Hakkinen 说：“哪支车队会做出这样的改变，他们又会向车迷们给出怎样的理由和说法呢？这将是一个重要因素。”
“如今这些车手在世界上都拥有庞大的粉丝群体，如果某支车队某天决定让某位车手当二号车手，车迷们会把这支车队骂上十字架。”
"所以，如今在激活这类车队指令时，你必须非常谨慎。"
'汉密尔顿在荷兰大奖赛上的情绪完全正常'
车队指令的问题在荷兰大奖赛上成为热议话题，当时汉密尔顿在被勒克莱尔阻挡后对法拉利车队感到愤怒。

汉密尔顿随后在社交媒体上发帖，对他在赞德沃特比赛期间向媒体和通过车队无线电发言时的语气表示遗憾，但哈基宁表示他的反应是“完全正常的”。
“我认为刘易斯在赞德沃特经历的一切，车队已经解释了为什么会发生这种情况，”哈基宁说。
“刘易斯（Lewis）所经历的那种情绪是绝对正常的。也许那不仅仅是情绪，也是常识。‘如果你让我超车，我们能拿到更多积分！’

“但如今当我从外部、当我置身围场之中观察大奖赛时，情况已经不同了。你能看到更多的东西，能获得更多关于正在发生的事情的信息。”
"车手们只能获得我们在电视上看到的极少一部分信息，所以当他们跟在另一辆车后面而对方不让超车时，他们没有车队所拥有的那些信息和计算数据，因此很多时候你会看到车手做出这类反应，这是很正常的。"
'Schumacher会在赛季首场比赛中就得到车队指令'
Hakkinen回顾了自己在争夺总冠军过程中经历车队指令的往事，这位芬兰车手曾与Michael Schumacher交锋，当时这位七届世界冠军在法拉利拥有明确的一号车手地位。
Hakkinen在1998年和1999年连续夺得车手总冠军，随后在2000年屈居Schumacher之后获得第二名，因为这位德国车手在法拉利赢得了他连续五个总冠军中的第一个。
“F1的车迷群体已经变了；如今这一代人和我那个时代不一样，”哈基宁说。
“当年我和在法拉利车队的迈克尔·舒马赫竞争时，他们从赛季的第一场比赛就开始使用车队指令了。”

“很明显，如果一支车队中有一位车手非常强势，开始赢得比赛、拿到积分，车队就会非常清楚：如果他们想赢得世界冠军，就必须百分之百地支持这位车手。”
“这就是迈克尔·舒马赫当年在法拉利效力时成功做到的事情。”
“我们在迈凯伦的理念则有些不同。我们希望给两位车手同样的机会，直到积分差距大到其中一方已经无法追上另一方；到那时，队友就必须开始支持领先的车手。这是一种常识性的运作方式。”
“现在车队们既想赢得车手总冠军，也想赢得车队总冠军，他们想两者兼得。所以，两位车手在每一场比赛中都始终保持最佳表现就非常重要。”

Two-time world champion Mika Hakkinen has warned that Formula 1 teams risk 'being crucified' by the sport's fans if they implement team orders in an attempt to influence this year's title battle.

Kimi Antonelli leads his Mercedes team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton by 59 points at the top of the standings, with McLaren's Lando Norris 83 points back in fourth after belatedly igniting his title defence with victories at the last two races.
With 11 rounds remaining, Hamilton is 28 points clear of his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc, while Norris has moved 55 points ahead of his McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri.

Given the significant margins by which the British duo each trail Antonelli, it has been a topic of speculation as to whether either Ferrari or McLaren would consider implementing team orders sooner rather than later to aid their better-positioned driver in the title fight.
Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix

Hakkinen, who spoke to Sky Sports News in his role as a Laureus Academy Member, said: "Which team is going to do this kind of change and what are the arguments they are going to give and tell the fans? This is going to be an important factor.
"All these drivers have a huge fanbase these days in the world, and if the team are going to decide one day that this driver is going to be number two, the fans are going to crucify this team.
"So, you have to be very careful these days how you are activating these kinds of team orders."
'Hamilton's Dutch GP emotion absolutely normal'
The issue of team orders became a talking point at the Dutch Grand Prix when Hamilton became infuriated with his Ferrari team after he was held by Leclerc.

After the race, Hamilton pointed out the contrast between the approaches of Ferrari and Mercedes, who were decisive in ordering Russell to let Antonelli past him having adjusted the Italian's strategy to fend off the threat coming from the seven-time world champion.
Lewis Hamilton outlined his frustrations after a fourth-place finish at the Dutch Grand Prix
Hamilton later posted on social media expressing regret for the tone of his comments to the media and over the radio during the Zandvoort race, but Hakkinen says his reaction was "absolutely normal".
"I think what Lewis experienced in Zandvoort, it was explained from the team why it happened," Hakkinen said.
"Emotions with Lewis' experience was absolutely normal. Maybe it wasn't only emotion, just also common sense. 'We can score more points if you let me overtake!'
Speaking on The Fast And The Curious podcast, Betty Glover, Christian Hewgill and Greg James reflect on their favourite radio messages from the Dutch GP
"But nowadays when I look at Grand Prix racing from the outside, when I'm in the paddock, it's different. You see much more, you get much more information on what's happening.

"The drivers are getting only a very tiny percentage of the information we get on TV, so when they are following another car and it doesn't let them overtake, they don't have the information and the calculations that the team have, so then very often you get these kind of reactions from the drivers, which is very normal."
'Schumacher would get team orders in first race of season'

Hakkinen reflected on his own experience of team orders during title races, with the Finnish driver having come up against Michael Schumacher when the seven-time world champion had clear number-one status at Ferrari.
Hakkinen won successive drivers' titles in 1998 and 1999 before finishing second to Schumacher in 2000 as the German won the first of five successive championships at Ferrari.
"The fanbase has changed in Formula 1; the generation is different than in my time," Hakkinen said.
"When I was racing against Michael Schumacher when he was at Ferrari, they started doing team orders already at the first race of the season.
Ferrari has unveiled its one-off livery, paying tribute to Michael Schumacher, for the Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix at Monza

"It was very obvious that if one driver is very strong in a team and started to win races and score points, the team is very much aware that if they want to win the world championship, they need to support this one driver 100 per cent.
"That's what Michael Schumacher was able to manage to do with Ferrari when he was racing there.

"We had a little bit of a different philosophy at McLaren. We wanted to give both drivers the same opportunity until the points were at a point that one couldn't catch the other; then the team-mate has to start supporting the leading driver. That was a common-sense operation.

"Now the teams want to win the Drivers' Championship and the Constructors' Championship, they want to win both. So. it's important that both drivers are getting maximum performance all the time in every race."
